attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT egress gateway for node2 and node3 on the private "lan" network (eth1, 10.50.50.0/24), implemented entirely via Ansible run from node4 (the designated control_node). node2/node3 got static LAN IPs with a default route via node1 preferred (lower metric) over the mgmt network. node1 got a static LAN address, a masquerade NAT source rule (10.50.50.0/24 -> eth0), and a forward-filter default-accept, with ip_forward already enabled. Verified end-to-end that node2/node3 reach the internet only via node1 (disabled the NAT rule, observed loss, restored it, observed recovery). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; each showed a changed OS boot_id and full recovery of its role (NAT/interface state on node1, static IP/route/egress on node2 and node3, working Ansible control and a clean idempotent playbook re-run on node4), with node2/node3 internet reachability reconfirmed after all four restarts.
